sources.entry: Better Resource Monitor - Lightweight macOS menu bar monitor for CPU, memory, storage, GPU, and network usage.

summary.one_liner: A lightweight, sandboxed macOS menu bar monitor that shows CPU, memory, storage, GPU, and network usage at a glance.
summary.what_it_does: Displays CPU, memory, storage, GPU, and network usage in the Mac menu bar. When "Show warning colors" is enabled, the tray turns orange if visible CPU, memory, or GPU usage reaches 81% or available storage drops below 10 GB; warning colors can be turned off from the tray menu. The README says the app is sandboxed, needs no admin password or root helper, makes zero network requests, and sends no telemetry. It is distributed through the Mac App Store (with automatic updates) and as a .dmg on GitHub Releases (manual updates). The README positions it as a low-overhead alternative to iStat Menus, Stats, and Eul, and it does not cover fan, temperature, or battery sensors.
use_cases: Quick daily check of Mac CPU and memory load
Watching free disk space from the menu bar
Monitoring GPU and network speed without opening Activity Monitor
Privacy-friendly system monitoring with no telemetry
how_to_run: Use pnpm dev for local testing (unsigned local builds are not a supported installed release)
notable: Sandboxed and requires no admin password or root helper
Zero network requests and no telemetry, per the README
Orange tray warning colors at 81% CPU/memory/GPU or under 10 GB free storage
Available on the Mac App Store as well as GitHub Releases (.dmg)
Supports Intel and Apple Silicon Macs on macOS 13 Ventura or newer
caveats: Does not monitor fan speed, temperatures, battery, or deep sensor history
GitHub .dmg builds have no automatic updates; the Mac App Store version does
keywords: see cpu and memory in menu bar
